title: new-affine-chart-section-ring-presentations-iso
statement:
theorem affine_chart_section_ring_presentations_iso
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (j : I) {A : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : A ⟶ Spec (R.obj j)) :
    IsIso (pullback.snd (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE
      ((OrderEmbedding.ofAntisymmetrization (α := {k : I // j ≤ k})).monotone.functor.obj
        (toAntisymmetrization (· ≤ ·) (⟨j, le_rfl⟩ : {k : I // j ≤ k}))).property))) g)

proof.text: Let k be the chosen representative of the antisymmetrization class of the upper-tail index (j, j ≤ j). The quotient representative law toAntisymmetrization_ofAntisymmetrization and Quotient.exact show that k and (j, j ≤ j) are related in both directions. In particular k.val ≤ j, while j ≤ k.val is k.property.

The preorder arrow homOfLE k.property is invertible, with inverse homOfLE of k.val ≤ j; both inverse equations hold because hom sets of the preorder category are subsingletons. Functoriality of R and of Scheme.Spec carries this isomorphism to Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE k.property)).
Apply Mathlib instance CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback_snd_iso_of_left_iso to the spectrum isomorphism and g. This proves that the displayed second pullback projection is an isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01ZR; elementary categorical proof using Mathlib quotient representatives, functoriality, and pullback of an isomorphism
